headline: Rain, Not Sri Lanka, Knocks Nepal Out of Asian Games Cricket
dek: Nepal topped its group unbeaten but exits after a no reserve day rule handed Sri Lanka the win by ranking.
body_markdown:
Nepal is out of the Asian Games cricket tournament in Japan. Rain washed out the men's quarterfinal against Sri Lanka on Monday, September 28, at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, and Nepal was eliminated without bowling a single ball, Nepal Khabar and Hamro Patro reported. Sri Lanka advances to the semifinal on ICC T20I ranking, both outlets said.

For a Nepali cricket fan, that is the whole story in one line. Nepal topped Group A unbeaten. The team walked into the quarterfinal in form. None of it mattered once the rain came, because the tournament runs on a rule that has nothing to do with runs or wickets.

Ratopati reported the match was set for 5:45am Nepal time at Korogi Sports Park, after Nepal finished as winners of Group A in the 20th Asian Games. The Kathmandu Post had reported before the match that the knockout stage carries no reserve day, so a total washout hands the win to the higher-ranked side, in this case Sri Lanka. Nepal's own head coach Stuart Law told the paper "You can't control the weather," and said conditions were not looking good for Nepal going into the game.

This was not the first time weather had decided a Nepal fixture this week. The Kathmandu Post reported that Nepal's final group match against Japan was also abandoned because of rain, though Nepal still advanced as group winner on points from earlier games.

## What the coverage missed

Nepal's exit fits a pattern the pre-match previews did not connect to Nepal's own fate. Sankalpa Khabar reported that two other quarterfinals this week had already been washed out, sending India and Pakistan through to the semifinal without playing a ball, on ICC ranking. Wikipedia's tournament page, accessed September 29, also records that no play was possible in Pakistan against Hong Kong and that Pakistan went through as the higher seeded team. Add Nepal's washout and rain and ranking, not cricket, decided three of this week's quarterfinals.

Ranking has settled a Games final before. Yahoo Sports reported that India's only previous men's cricket gold at the Games, at Hangzhou in 2023, also came down to the no reserve day rule. Afghanistan had batted and reached 112 for 5 in 18.2 overs when rain ended the final with no result, ESPNcricinfo's scorecard shows. India, who had not batted, won gold as the side ranked higher.

The format works against Nepal twice over, not once. ESPNcricinfo's match preview noted that three of the last four games in this tournament had already ended without a toss. Wikipedia's tournament page also shows the top four ICC-ranked teams received automatic byes straight into the quarterfinals, skipping the group stage. Nepal, ranked lower, had to win through a three-team preliminary group first, then went out on the same ranking rule that had already carried India and Pakistan through.

Nepal and Sri Lanka have lost a scheduled match to rain before. ESPNcricinfo reported that the two sides' last meeting, at the 2024 T20 World Cup, "was washed out without even the toss." Monday's result is the second time in two years these two teams have failed to play a scheduled game against each other.

## What we still do not know

No outlet has reported whether the Cricket Association of Nepal, the Asian Cricket Council or the Olympic Council of Asia will review the no reserve day rule after it decided Nepal's exit and two other quarterfinals in the same week.

Whether coach Stuart Law or the Cricket Association of Nepal lodged any formal protest with tournament organisers, beyond his comments to reporters, has not been reported.

key_facts.fact: Nepal was eliminated from the Asian Games cricket quarterfinal against Sri Lanka after rain washed out the match on September 28, without a ball bowled.
Sri Lanka advanced to the semifinal on ICC T20I ranking after the washout, not on the field.
The quarterfinal had no reserve day built in, so a total washout was decided by ranking alone.
Nepal finished Group A unbeaten and topped the group before the quarterfinal.
Two other quarterfinals this week were also washed out, sending India and Pakistan through without playing a ball.
Afghanistan had reached 112 for 5 in 18.2 overs when rain stopped the 2023 Asian Games final, and India won gold on ICC ranking without batting.

nepali.headline: वर्षाले एसियाड क्रिकेटबाट नेपाल बाहिर, श्रीलंका र्याङ्किङमा अघि
nepali.dek: नेपाल समूह 'ए'मा अपराजित शीर्ष स्थानमा रहे पनि रिजर्भ डे नहुँदा श्रीलंका र्याङ्किङका भरमा सेमिफाइनलमा पुगेको छ।
nepali.take: नेपाल श्रीलंकासँग हारेन, नियमसँग हार्यो। नेपालखबर र हाम्रोपात्रोका अनुसार टोली एक बल पनि नखेली एसियाली खेलकुदबाट बाहिरिएको छ। रिजर्भ डे नभएकाले श्रीलंका र्याङ्किङका भरमा अघि बढेको द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। "मौसम कसैको नियन्त्रणमा हुँदैन," नेपालका मुख्य प्रशिक्षक स्टुअर्ट लले खेलअघि द काठमाडौं पोस्टसँग भनेका थिए। संकल्प खबरका अनुसार यो हप्ता भारत र पाकिस्तान पनि रद्द खेलबाटै अघि बढे। नेपाल वायरको गणनाअनुसार यो हप्ता तीन क्वार्टरफाइनल क्रिकेटले होइन, वर्षा र र्याङ्किङले टुंगिए। अर्को एसियाली खेलकुदअघि नेपाल क्रिकेट संघले यो नियम बदल्न दबाब दिन्छ कि दिँदैन, त्यो खबर आएको छैन।
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं । जापानमा जारी एसियाली खेलकुदको पुरुष क्रिकेट प्रतियोगितामा नेपाल क्वार्टरफाइनलबाट बाहिरिएको छ। निसिनस्थित कोरोगी स्पोर्ट्स पार्कमा सोमबार (२८ सेप्टेम्बर) हुनुपर्ने नेपाल र श्रीलंकाबीचको खेल वर्षाका कारण हुनै नसकेको नेपालखबर र हाम्रोपात्रोले जनाएका छन्। नेपाल एउटै बल नखेली प्रतियोगिताबाट बाहिरिएको पनि दुवैले लेखेका छन्। आईसीसी टी-२० र्याङ्किङमा माथि रहेको श्रीलंका सेमिफाइनलमा पुगेको दुवै सञ्चारमाध्यमले लेखेका छन्। आईसीसी क्रिकेटको विश्व निकाय हो।

नेपाली क्रिकेट प्रेमीले बुझ्ने कुरा यत्ति हो। नेपालले समूह 'ए'मा एउटै खेल नहारी अपराजित च्याम्पियन बनेको थियो। टोली राम्रो लयमा क्वार्टरफाइनलमा उत्रिएको थियो। तर वर्षा परेपछि यी सबैको कुनै अर्थ रहेन। प्रतियोगिता चल्ने नियमको रन वा विकेटसँग कुनै साइनो छैन।

२०औं एसियाली खेलकुदको समूह 'ए' विजेता बनेको नेपालको खेल कोरोगी स्पोर्ट्स पार्कमा नेपाली समयअनुसार बिहान पौने ६ बजे हुने तालिका रहेको रातोपातीले जनाएको थियो। नकआउट चरणमा रिजर्भ डे नहुने द काठमाडौं पोस्टले खेलअघि जनाएको थियो। पोस्टका अनुसार खेल पूरै वर्षाले रद्द भए र्याङ्किङमा माथिको टोली विजयी हुन्छ, र यस पटक त्यो टोली श्रीलंका थियो। "मौसम कसैको नियन्त्रणमा हुँदैन," नेपालका मुख्य प्रशिक्षक स्टुअर्ट लले पोस्टसँग भनेका थिए। खेलअघि मौसम नेपालको पक्षमा नदेखिएको पनि उनले पोस्टलाई बताएका थिए।

यो हप्ता मौसमले नेपालको खेल टुंगो लगाएको यो पहिलो पटक होइन। जापानविरुद्धको नेपालको अन्तिम समूह खेल पनि वर्षाका कारण रद्द भएको द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। तर अघिल्ला खेलका अंकका आधारमा नेपाल समूह विजेता बनेर अघि बढेको पोस्टले लेखेको छ।

## समाचारले छुटाएको कुरा

नेपाल बाहिरिनु एक्लो घटना होइन। खेलअघिका पूर्वावलोकनले यो ढाँचालाई नेपालको आफ्नै भाग्यसँग जोडेका थिएनन्। यो हप्ता अरू दुई क्वार्टरफाइनल पनि वर्षाले रद्द भएको संकल्प खबरले जनाएको छ। ती खेलमा भारत र पाकिस्तान एक बल नखेली आईसीसी र्याङ्किङका भरमा सेमिफाइनल पुगेको पनि संकल्प खबरले लेखेको छ। २९ सेप्टेम्बरमा हेरिएको विकिपिडियाको प्रतियोगिता पृष्ठले पाकिस्तान र हङकङबीच कुनै खेल हुन नसकेको देखाउँछ। माथिल्लो वरीयताका कारण पाकिस्तान अघि बढेको पनि सोही पृष्ठमा उल्लेख छ। नेपालको खेल पनि जोड्दा यो हप्ताका तीन क्वार्टरफाइनलको नतिजा क्रिकेटले होइन, वर्षा र र्याङ्किङले तय गर्यो।

र्याङ्किङले यसअघि एसियाली खेलकुदको फाइनल पनि टुंगो लगाएको छ। सन् २०२३ मा हाङ्झाउमा भारतले जितेको एकमात्र पुरुष क्रिकेट स्वर्ण पनि रिजर्भ डे नहुने नियमबाटै टुंगिएको याहू स्पोर्ट्सले जनाएको छ। इएसपीएनक्रिकइन्फोको स्कोरकार्डअनुसार अफगानिस्तानले १८.२ ओभरमा ५ विकेटमा ११२ रन बनाएका बेला वर्षाका कारण फाइनल नतिजाविहीन भयो। ब्याटिङ नगरेको भारतले र्याङ्किङमा माथि भएकाले स्वर्ण जितेको पनि स्कोरकार्डमा उल्लेख छ।

यो ढाँचाले नेपाललाई एक होइन, दुई ठाउँमा घाटा पुर्याउँछ। यो प्रतियोगितामा पछिल्ला चार खेलमध्ये तीन टस नै नभई सकिएको इएसपीएनक्रिकइन्फोको खेल पूर्वावलोकनले उल्लेख गरेको छ। आईसीसी र्याङ्किङका शीर्ष चार टोलीले समूह चरण नखेली सिधै क्वार्टरफाइनल पाएको विकिपिडियाको प्रतियोगिता पृष्ठले देखाउँछ। तल्लो र्याङ्किङको नेपालले भने पहिले तीन टोलीको प्रारम्भिक समूह जित्नुपर्यो। त्यसपछि भारत र पाकिस्तानलाई अघि बढाएकै र्याङ्किङ नियमले नेपाललाई बाहिर पार्यो।

नेपाल र श्रीलंकाबीचको खेल यसअघि पनि वर्षाले खोसेको छ। सन् २०२४ को टी-२० विश्वकपमा दुई टोलीको पछिल्लो भेट "टससमेत नभई वर्षाका कारण रद्द भएको" इएसपीएनक्रिकइन्फोले लेखेको छ। दुई वर्षमा यी दुई टोलीबीचको तालिकाबद्ध खेल नहुनु सोमबारको घटनासहित दोस्रो पटक हो।

## अझै थाहा नभएका कुरा

नेपाल क्रिकेट संघ, एसियाली क्रिकेट परिषद् वा एसियाली ओलम्पिक परिषद्ले रिजर्भ डे नहुने नियमको समीक्षा गर्छन् कि गर्दैनन्, कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले जनाएको छैन। यही नियमले एकै हप्तामा नेपालसहित तीन क्वार्टरफाइनलको नतिजा तय गरेको छ।

प्रशिक्षक स्टुअर्ट ल वा नेपाल क्रिकेट संघले पत्रकारसँगको टिप्पणीबाहेक आयोजकसमक्ष औपचारिक विरोध दर्ता गरे कि गरेनन्, त्यो पनि सार्वजनिक भएको छैन।

caption.body:
सोमबार (२८ सेप्टेम्बर) वर्षाका कारण श्रीलंकाविरुद्धको क्वार्टरफाइनल हुनै सकेन। नेपाल एउटै बल नखेली बाहिरिएको नेपालखबर र हाम्रोपात्रोले जनाएका छन्। श्रीलंका भने आईसीसी र्याङ्किङका भरमा अघि बढेको दुवैले लेखेका छन्।

यो प्रतियोगितामा वर्षाले रद्द भएको नकआउट खेलका लागि रिजर्भ डे नहुने द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। "मौसम कसैको नियन्त्रणमा हुँदैन," नेपालका मुख्य प्रशिक्षक स्टुअर्ट लले खेलअघि द काठमाडौं पोस्टसँग भनेका थिए।

यो हप्ता यही नियमले टुंगो लगाएको यो पहिलो खेल होइन। अरू दुई क्वार्टरफाइनल पनि वर्षाले रद्द हुँदा भारत र पाकिस्तान यसैगरी अघि बढेको संकल्प खबरले जनाएको छ। सन् २०२३ को एसियाली खेलकुदको पुरुष फाइनल पनि वर्षापछि र्याङ्किङका आधारमा टुंगिएको याहू स्पोर्ट्सले लेखेको छ।

नेपाल क्रिकेट संघले रिजर्भ डे माग्छ कि माग्दैन, कुनै सञ्चारमाध्यमले जनाएको छैन। श्रीलंका सेमिफाइनल खेल्नेछ। नेपाल एउटै बल नखेली घर फर्कँदैछ।
caption.trigger: मौसम कसैको वशमा नहुँदा र्याङ्किङका भरमा नतिजा दिने यो नियम उचित हो, कि नकआउटमा रिजर्भ डे नै चाहिनुपर्छ?

nepali.editor: A body sentence and a caption sentence carry Kathmandu Post facts with no source, which fails record fidelity. Several sentences also carry grammar errors, and the take has a clause built like translated English, all of which must be fixed before publishing.

image_brief.alt_text: An empty cricket pitch covered by rain tarpaulins under a grey sky, evoking the washed out Nepal versus Sri Lanka Asian Games quarterfinal.

angles.claim: The Nepal-Sri Lanka quarterfinal has already been decided by rain, not just risked: multiple Nepali outlets report Nepal is out of the tournament without a ball bowled, and Sri Lanka advances to the semi-final on ICC ranking.
angles.why_it_matters: The story as briefed frames this as a live jeopardy piece ('Nepal faces Sri Lanka today'), but the outcome readers actually need — elimination, not suspense — is already public from same-day Nepali reporting and is the first thing Nepal Wire should lead with rather than repeat the pre-match frame.

evidence.fact: Reports the Sri Lanka match was cancelled by rain and Nepal is out of the quarterfinal without having played, with Sri Lanka through by ranking.
Headline and text state Nepal is out of the Asiad quarterfinal without a single ball played due to rain, and Sri Lanka has gone through to the semifinal on ICC ranking.
Reports that two quarterfinals were already washed out this week and India and Pakistan advanced to the semifinal without playing a ball, on ICC ranking.

angles.claim: This is not an isolated weather accident: the same 'no reserve day, higher-ranked team advances' rule has now decided three of the tournament's four men's quarterfinals in a row, and it also decided the previous Asian Games cricket gold medal in 2023.
angles.why_it_matters: Framing Nepal's exit as bad luck on one morning misses that the format itself has now produced washout-decided results repeatedly within the same week, and did so in the prior edition of the Games — a structural, recurring failure of tournament design that Nepali coverage has not connected to Nepal's own elimination.

evidence.fact: Quarterfinal 1 (Pakistan v Hong Kong, 28 September): 'No play was possible due to rain... Pakistan advanced by virtue of being the higher-seeded team.'
India's only prior Asian Games cricket gold, at Hangzhou in 2023, was awarded when rain washed out the final against Afghanistan and India held the higher ICC ranking.
'The last four games in the competition have had three washouts without the toss taking place, and one was abandoned after 15 overs.'

angles.claim: The tournament's seeding rules already shield the strongest cricket boards before any rain falls: the four highest-ranked ICC teams get automatic byes straight into the quarterfinals, while lower-ranked sides such as Nepal must first survive a rain-exposed round-robin group.
angles.why_it_matters: Coverage treats the no-reserve-day rule as the whole story, but the format doubly protects top-ranked boards — first by letting them skip the group stage entirely, then by handing them the win on any knockout washout — a compounding advantage for the same teams that Nepali previews have not spelled out.

evidence.fact: The top four highest-seeded teams by ICC ranking received automatic byes into the quarterfinals, while Nepal had to win through a three-team preliminary group first.
Under Olympic Council of Asia and Asian Cricket Council regulations, a washed-out knockout game is 'settled by seedings alone' with no reserve day built in.

angles.claim: Rain has washed out a scheduled Nepal-Sri Lanka international before: their last meeting, at the 2024 T20 World Cup, was also abandoned without a toss, making today's washout the second time in two years these two sides have failed to play a scheduled game.
angles.why_it_matters: This specific rivalry has a documented weather record that none of the Nepali previews mention; it shows the Nagoya/Nisshin rain risk this week was not an unforeseeable fluke for this exact fixture.

evidence.fact: 'The last time Nepal and Sri Lanka were slated to take each other on in a T20I fixture (at the 2024 T20 World Cup), it was washed out without even the toss.'

unanswered.question: Will the Cricket Association of Nepal, the Asian Cricket Council or the Olympic Council of Asia review the no-reserve-day, ranking-tiebreaker rule after it has now decided three of four men's quarterfinals in the same week, including Nepal's own exit?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) leadership, Asian Cricket Council, Olympic Council of Asia technical committee

unanswered.question: Did coach Stuart Law or CAN lodge any formal protest or request with tournament organisers before or after Nepal's elimination, beyond his remarks to journalists in Nagoya?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Stuart Law, Cricket Association of Nepal

unanswered.question: How much government or Nepal Sports Council funding was allocated to the men's cricket team's Asian Games campaign, and does that compare to preparation time or resources given to higher-ranked sides who received byes?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepal Sports Council, Cricket Association of Nepal, Ministry of Youth and Sports

unanswered.question: Does the ICC or ACC see any problem in a team advancing on ICC T20I ranking while fielding a weakened or second-string squad at the event itself, as Sri Lanka reportedly did with regulars on England duty?
unanswered.who_could_answer: International Cricket Council, Sri Lanka Cricket

investigation.summary: Nepal Wire can report what the pre-match previews could not: same-day Nepali outlets already show the Sri Lanka quarterfinal was washed out with Nepal eliminated without bowling a ball, and this is the third of four Asiad quarterfinals this week decided that way, echoing the same rule that handed India the 2023 Hangzhou gold. No coverage in the candidate set connects Nepal's exit to that pattern, to the seeding structure that already favours top-ranked boards before any rain falls, or to the identical washout that voided Nepal and Sri Lanka's last scheduled meeting in 2024.

findings.passage: Yahoo Sports reported that India's only previous cricket gold at the Games, at Hangzhou in 2023, was awarded the same way, when rain washed out the final against Afghanistan and India held the higher ICC ranking.
findings.problem: The 2023 Hangzhou final was not a zero-play washout like the events this piece compares it to. Afghanistan batted and reached 112 for 5 in 18.2 overs before rain ended play; India, who had not batted, won gold on ranking. ESPNcricinfo's own scorecard and Olympics.com record overs bowled and runs scored. Presenting this as the same kind of event as Nepal's 'eliminated without bowling a single ball' exit overstates how identical the pattern is, which matters because the whole missed section leans on this being a repeated, structurally identical failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the sentence to note Afghanistan batted and scored runs before rain ended the 2023 final without a result, and that India then won on ranking. Keep the pattern point but do not equate it to a zero-ball washout.

findings.passage: That rule has now decided three of four quarterfinals this week, Sankalpa Khabar and Wikipedia's tournament record show.
findings.problem: Sankalpa Khabar is cited elsewhere only for the India and Pakistan washouts, two of the four quarterfinals. The 'three of four' tally is the newsroom's own arithmetic, reached by adding Nepal's separately reported elimination, as the body itself honestly frames it: 'Add Nepal's washout and three of the round's four quarterfinals were decided.' The take instead states that Sankalpa Khabar and Wikipedia 'show' the three of four figure directly, which neither source states as a combined total.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the take to something like: 'Add Nepal's own exit and three of the round's four quarterfinals were decided by rain and ranking, not cricket, Nepal Wire's count of Sankalpa Khabar's and Wikipedia's separate reports shows.' Do not let the sources appear to state the combined total themselves.

findings.passage: Wikipedia's record of the tournament, citing the official fixtures, confirms one of those games, Pakistan against Hong Kong, where "no play was possible due to rain" and Pakistan advanced "by virtue of being the higher seeded team."
findings.problem: A live, editable encyclopedia entry is used as the sole named source for a direct quotation in the article's central 'what the coverage missed' argument, with no version, revision date, or permalink given. Wikipedia text on an in-progress or just-finished tournament can be edited or corrected within hours, which would leave this quote unverifiable to a reader checking the link later.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the underlying news agency or tournament report that Wikipedia itself footnotes for the Pakistan versus Hong Kong result, or add an accessed-on date and note Wikipedia as a secondary confirmation rather than the sole named source for a quoted claim.

findings.passage: Cricket Association of Nepal has not said whether it will push organisers to fix the format before the next Games.
findings.problem: This reads as an affirmative claim that CAN was asked and stayed silent. The body's own, more careful framing in 'What we still do not know' only says the question 'is not yet answered by any of those bodies', meaning no outlet has reported an answer, not that CAN was approached and declined to respond. The take overstates this into a specific non-response by a named body, which is a harder claim to defend.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the take to the body's framing: 'Whether Cricket Association of Nepal will push to change the rule before the next Games has not been reported.'

findings.passage: If a rulebook, not a bowler, ends your team's medal run, is that still a fair result?
findings.problem: The trigger is framed so nearly every reader will answer the same way, no. The house style requires a genuine side picking question where both answers rest on the record; this one assumes the conclusion the piece already argues, which makes it engagement bait rather than a real fork.
findings.suggested_fix: Try a genuinely two sided version, e.g., 'Should a format that has already ended three of four quarterfinals this week be scrapped, or is ranking a fair tiebreak when nobody can control the weather?' or leave the trigger empty per the two in five rule.

findings.passage: eliminated without bowling a single ball ... the higher-ranked side, in this case Sri Lanka
findings.problem: House style bans hyphens inside sentences except for standard compound words like well known. 'higher-ranked', 'lower-ranked' and 'top-ranked' recur through the body and investigation section and are closer to constructed compounds than fixed dictionary terms.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'the side ranked higher' or similar to avoid the hyphenated compound, consistent with the punctuation rule.

findings.passage: How much Nepal Sports Council money went into the team's Asian Games campaign, and whether that compares fairly to the preparation time given to higher ranked sides who skipped the group stage entirely, remains unanswered.
findings.problem: This unanswered question introduces a funding fairness angle with no supporting reporting anywhere in the sources list, and no indication anyone asked the Nepal Sports Council. It risks reading as an implied accusation of underfunding with zero record behind it, even though it is framed as a question.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop this question or narrow it to what is actually known, such as noting no public account of the campaign's budget exists, without implying an unfair comparison the record does not support.

red_team.summary: The piece correctly leads with the confirmed elimination and is timely and well sourced for its core facts, but the investigation section stretches its strongest comparison, the 2023 Hangzhou final, into a closer parallel than the record supports since that match saw overs bowled and runs scored before rain intervened. The take then hardens a newsroom calculated tally and an absence of reporting into claims that read as sourced or affirmative when they are not, and the sole reliance on a live Wikipedia page for a quoted claim is a defensibility weak point. The caption's trigger question is one sided rather than a genuine fork, which will cost engagement quality even though the headline and hook are otherwise sharp and compliant with the card standard.

responses.response: The red team is right. Afghanistan batted and scored runs in the 2023 final before rain ended play, which is a materially different event from a zero-ball washout. Presenting it as the same pattern overstates the parallel that the missed section leans on.
responses.proposed_edit: Yahoo Sports reported that India's only previous cricket gold at the Games, at Hangzhou in 2023, also came down to the no reserve day rule. Afghanistan had batted and reached 112 for 5 in 18.2 overs when rain ended the final with no result, and India, who had not batted, won gold on ICC ranking.

responses.response: The take sentence does attribute the combined three of four figure to the two named sources as if they state it together, while the body correctly frames it as the newsroom's own addition. That inconsistency is a real accuracy problem in the take.
responses.proposed_edit: Add Nepal's own exit and three of the round's four quarterfinals were decided by rain and ranking, not cricket, based on Nepal Wire's count of Sankalpa Khabar's and Wikipedia's separate reports.

responses.response: A live wiki page as the sole named source for a direct quote is a real verification risk, since the text can change after publication with no way for a reader to check what the article saw. The safer path is to lean on Wikipedia's own footnoted source or note an access date.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the passage to: "Wikipedia's tournament page, accessed September 29 and citing agency wire reports, confirms one of those games, Pakistan against Hong Kong, where no play was possible due to rain and Pakistan advanced by virtue of being the higher seeded team."

responses.response: The take states CAN's silence as if the association was asked and did not answer, but the body's own careful framing only says no outlet has reported an answer. The take should match the more precise body language.
responses.proposed_edit: Whether Cricket Association of Nepal will push to change the rule before the next Games has not been reported.

responses.response: The trigger as written invites near unanimous agreement, which fails the house style requirement for a genuine fork where both sides rest on the record.
responses.proposed_edit: Should a format that has already decided three of four quarterfinals this week by rain and ranking be scrapped, or is ranking a fair tiebreak when nobody can control the weather?

responses.response: House style bans hyphens inside sentences but explicitly exempts compound words that need a hyphen in standard spelling. 'Higher-ranked,' 'lower-ranked' and 'top-ranked' are standard English compound adjectives before a noun, the same category as other accepted technical compounds, not a stylistic dash used mid-sentence for rhythm or aside. Rewriting every instance as 'the side ranked higher' throughout a piece this dense with rankings would make the prose clunkier without fixing a real punctuation violation.
responses.proposed_edit: No change needed. If the judge disagrees, the minimal fix is limited to the two instances flagged, not a full pass through the piece: 'the side ranked higher, in this case Sri Lanka.'

responses.response: This question has zero reporting behind it anywhere in the sources list and edges toward implying underfunding or unfairness by the Nepal Sports Council with no documented record. That is close to an invented implication, which the house rules forbid even in question form.
responses.proposed_edit: No public account of what the Asian Games campaign cost, or how that compared to preparation time for higher seeded teams who skipped the group stage, has been reported.

defense.summary: Five of seven findings are accepted because they identify real gaps between what the sources support and what the article's take and body claim: the 2023 final comparison overstates equivalence to a zero-ball washout, the take's 'three of four' and CAN silence lines outrun the body's more careful hedges, the Wikipedia quote needs firmer sourcing, and the trigger question is one sided engagement bait. The funding question is dropped as unsupported speculation. The hyphenation finding is contested because house style's own exception for standard compound words covers 'higher-ranked' and similar terms, and rewriting them throughout would hurt readability without curing a genuine punctuation violation.
